title: Insulin Fundamentals & Calculations
description: Meal coverage, background insulin and the language of a prescription.
faq: When should I ask for a settings review?
Bring repeated patterns and the circumstances around them to your diabetes team.
Can I enter my glucose to get a dose here?
The walkthroughs use fixed classroom examples. There is no personal dosing tool.
What should I take to an education visit?
Bring your current written plan, the actual devices you use and a question about a recent meal.

title: Glucose Patterns & Body Physiology
description: Read the sequence of events behind a rise or a low.
faq: How many traces should I compare?
Compare several similar days for a routine review. An urgent symptom needs attention immediately.
Which notes give a curve context?
Meal timing, activity, illness, insulin delivery and whether the sensor signal was reliable.
Can a model trace diagnose my pattern?
It shows one possible sequence. Your clinician can help assess your actual readings.

title: Insulin Administration & Injection Care
description: Get familiar with delivery devices, sites and storage.
faq: Which instructions apply to my device?
Match the product name, strength and model to the manufacturer’s instructions and your clinic training.
Who can watch me practise?
Ask a diabetes educator or nurse to observe your technique with your usual equipment.
What if a dose or delivery is uncertain?
Use your written backup instructions or seek clinical advice rather than guessing how much was delivered.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring & Diabetes Technology
description: Understand a sensor trace and the devices behind it.
faq: Why does a report need a date range?
A snapshot, a day and a multiweek summary answer different questions. Check dates and missing data.
What if a reading does not fit my symptoms?
Follow your device’s meter-confirmation instructions and your care plan.
Where are my actual device settings?
Open Devices & Data Sources for GlucoNest connections. The examples here use illustrative data.

title: Food, Nutrition & Indian Carb Counting
description: Explore labels, katoris, home recipes and mixed meals.
faq: How can I estimate a home recipe?
Identify the carbohydrate-containing ingredients, estimate the batch total and divide by actual cooked yield.
Where do the example foods come from?
The estimator uses GlucoNest’s existing Indian Food Library entries and shows their recorded sources. They are recipe estimates.
Why do two servings with the same name differ?
Portion, water content, grain, fillings and cooking methods can all vary.

title: Exercise, Sports & Physical Activity
description: Explore activity, recovery and preparations for the next session.
faq: What changes the response to the same session?
Starting glucose, active insulin, intensity, food, sleep and recent activity can all matter.
What belongs in a sports plan?
Agree on monitoring, fast carbohydrate, access to help, stopping criteria and follow-up after activity.
Can I use the example chart to change insulin?
No. It illustrates possible directions; adjustments belong in an individual exercise plan.

title: Sick Days, Ketones & Emergencies
description: Official guidance on illness, ketones and getting urgent help.

title: Mental Health & Living with T1D
description: Make room for distress, relationships and support.
faq: Who can I talk to first?
A trusted member of the diabetes team, primary-care clinician or mental health professional can help plan support.
How can I make an appointment easier?
Write down one situation that felt difficult and the kind of help you would like. You can bring a supporter.
Can peers replace a clinical safety plan?
Peers can offer understanding and practical questions. Keep a clinical plan for insulin, illness and emergencies.

title: Long-Term Health & Preventive Care
description: Learn what each check measures and what to ask at review.
faq: When should I book screening?
Age, diabetes duration, pregnancy, symptoms and earlier findings influence timing. Confirm your own schedule with the clinic.
Does screening only matter when I have symptoms?
Some early changes cause few symptoms. Scheduled checks can identify them sooner.
What should I ask after a test?
Ask what the result means, whether it needs confirming and who will arrange the next step.

title: T1D Across Different Life Stages
description: Care from childhood through adulthood, pregnancy and later life.
faq: Should glucose targets be the same throughout life?
Goals can change with development, pregnancy, health, support and the risk of a low.
How can support change without taking over?
Ask which tasks the person wants to handle, which to share and when help is needed.
What helps at a transition between teams?
Arrange a named contact and bring a current plan, device details and outstanding questions.

title: Advanced T1D Science & Research
description: Read an evidence claim, from beta cells to trials and approvals.
faq: How can I tell what evidence a claim describes?
Check whether it comes from a laboratory, a clinical trial or a regulator. Read the date, population and outcome.
Does approval travel between countries?
Regulators approve specific indications in their own jurisdictions. Local availability is a separate question.
What belongs in a specialist discussion?
Bring the study or label and ask about eligibility, known harms, alternatives and length of follow-up.

title: Practical Everyday T1D Life
description: Plan for travel, changing weather, shared meals and work.
faq: Why check local arrangements?
Supply brands, insurance rules, disposal services and travel procedures vary between places.
What makes a backup plan usable?
Keep exact product names, clinic contacts and a way to monitor glucose readily accessible.
How can I prepare without sharing my entire record?
Give helpers the minimum information they need for their agreed role and emergency response.
